forces.title: Branded jewellers aggressively expand stores, driving revenue growth and market share.
forces.description: Leading branded jewellers are significantly expanding their retail footprint, with sample players adding over 300 new stores in FY26. This aggressive expansion strategy, often via the franchisee route to mitigate inventory funding, is a key driver for projected revenue growth of ~35% in FY26 and 20-25% in FY27, enabling market share gains from the unorganised sector.

forces.title: Expanding middle class and HNIs drive increasing demand for gems and jewellery.
forces.description: India's demographic trends, including a rapidly growing middle class and affluent consumers, are significant demand drivers. By 2036, the middle class and affluent are projected to account for 93% of all spending, up from 80% in 2026. India also holds 3.7% of global HNIs, with over 85,000 individuals worth above Rs. 85 crore, bolstering demand for luxury goods.

forces.title: Luxury consumer base contracts, shifting spending towards experiences and preowned goods.
forces.description: The luxury consumer base continued to contract in 2025, with an estimated 20 million fewer consumers than in 2024. This trend is characterized by shoppers reducing purchase frequency, opting for smaller indulgences, trading down, or re-directing spending towards experiences and preowned luxury items. This indicates a challenging environment for primary luxury goods sales, requiring brands to adapt.

forces.title: US reciprocal tariffs severely impact gems and jewellery exports, causing significant decline.
forces.description: Labour-intensive categories, including gems and jewellery, are facing significant pressure from US reciprocal tariffs. Gems and jewellery exports fell by 15.6% in Sep-Oct 2025, with a sharp 70% decline in shipments to the US. While strong growth to alternative markets like UAE and Hong Kong somewhat mitigated this, the overall impact on US-bound exports is substantial, necessitating market diversification.

forces.title: Structural shift: gold consumption leans investment, less volume for jewellery.
forces.description: Global and Indian gold consumption is undergoing a structural shift. Jewellery's share has fallen significantly to ~33% globally and below 60% in India, well below long-term averages. Investment demand, particularly gold ETFs and bar-and-coin buying, has surged due to safe-haven demand and diversification motives, influencing overall gold allocation away from discretionary jewellery purchases by volume.

forces.title: Regulatory support and international trade agreements enhance gems and jewellery exports.
forces.description: The sector benefits significantly from favorable government policies, including 100% FDI under the automatic route and the presence of 10 special economic zones. Crucially, trade agreements like CEPA with the UAE (targeting US$70 billion exports by 2030), Australia eliminating tariffs, and the India-UK FTA (projecting doubled exports to UK by 2027) provide substantial competitive advantages and market access.

forces.title: Secondhand luxury market growth outpaces new luxury, driven by consumer interest and tech.
forces.description: The secondhand luxury goods market is experiencing rapid growth, estimated to reach €50 billion in 2025 with a 4-6% rise, outpacing sales of new luxury items. This growth is fueled by consumer enthusiasm for 'treasure hunting,' iconic archival pieces, and enhanced trust from innovations like AI-powered authentication tools and digital product passports, indicating a significant shift in consumer behavior and market dynamics.

forces.title: Elevated gold prices increase jewellers' inventory holding requirements, raising funding needs.
forces.description: Sustained high gold prices, coupled with continued store additions by jewellers, have led to a marked increase in inventory holding requirements. The median inventory holding for sample jewellers rose to 207 days in H1FY26 from 186 days in H1FY25. This escalates working capital funding needs, potentially requiring incremental borrowings despite higher profitability from inventory gains.

forces.title: Watches face pressure from alternative investments, secondhand market, and smart devices.
forces.description: The watches segment is under severe pressure as consumers become more rational. A shift in preferences towards other investment assets, the growing availability of secondhand alternatives, and the increasing appeal of sporty and smart-device alternatives are drawing demand away from traditional watches. This confluence of factors contributes to significant declines in watch sales.

forces.title: Foreign luxury brands face intensifying competition from local Chinese players.
forces.description: In Mainland China, international luxury brands face intensifying competition from local players across categories. This is driven by rising cultural pride and confidence, fueling the success of Chinese brands that offer better value for money and culturally resonant propositions, particularly appealing to younger consumers. This dynamic contributes to the overall market slowdown for foreign luxury goods.

forces.title: RBI eases gold metal loan guidelines, boosting funding avenues for non-manufacturing jewellers.
forces.description: The Reserve Bank of India has amended its guidelines for gold metal loans, now extending this borrowing avenue to non-manufacturing jewellers. This move aims to harmonise gold funding options and is expected to provide greater financial flexibility and access to capital for a broader range of jewellery businesses, particularly those focused on retail and trading, supporting their operational needs.

forces.title: Accelerated formalisation of jewellery sector shifts consumer preference to branded players.
forces.description: The gems and jewellery sector is experiencing accelerated formalisation, driven by shifting consumer preferences towards branded jewellers and regulatory interventions (e.g., mandatory hallmarking). This trend enables organised players to gain significant market share from the traditionally unorganised sector, contributing to their strong projected revenue growth and increased store additions.

forces.title: Consumers prioritize value preservation, boosting fine jewellery as an asset class.
forces.description: In the luxury market, consumers increasingly prioritize value preservation, leading to a strong gravitation towards fine jewellery purchases. The increasing price of rare metals further reinforces jewellery's appeal as an investment asset. This trend positively impacts the jewellery segment, differentiating it from other luxury categories that may not offer similar long-term asset value.

forces.title: Gems and jewellery exports diversify to non-US markets due to tariff pressures.
forces.description: Due to the impact of US reciprocal tariffs, India's gems and jewellery exports are showing early signs of structural reorientation. Exports to the US declined sharply, while growth to the UAE (5%) and Hong Kong (14.2%) significantly mitigated the overall decline. This indicates a strategic shift towards diversifying export destinations, which will be a key monitorable trend in the coming months.

viewpoints.title: Branded jewellers project robust revenue growth, market share gains in FY26-27.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings forecasts ~35% revenue growth for branded jewellers in FY26 and 20-25% in FY27. This strong momentum is driven by aggressive store expansion, accelerated formalisation of the sector, and sustained consumer appetite despite rising gold prices. Operating profit margins are also expected to expand, albeit normalizing later, signaling a healthy outlook for organized players.

viewpoints.title: Jewellery category strongly improves in China's luxury market, driven by value preservation.
viewpoints.description: The jewellery category in mainland China showed significant improvement in 2025, with its expected decrease narrowing to 0-5%. Consumers, particularly those focused on value preservation, gravitated towards jewellery purchases, especially fine jewellery. The rising prices of rare metals further bolstered the asset value perception of jewellery, contrasting with other luxury segments facing pressure.

viewpoints.title: Global watch market shows polarized yet broadly stable performance, with resilience at price extremes.
viewpoints.description: The global watches segment demonstrated a polarized performance across various players and price points in 2025, but remained broadly stable overall. Resilience was observed at both the high and entry ends of the market. The secondary market for watches also remained active, as factors like tariffs and high retail prices pushed some consumers towards preowned alternatives, influencing market dynamics.

viewpoints.title: Indian jewellery market shows value resilience, but volume shifts to lighter, lower-carat.
viewpoints.description: Indian jewellery purchases rose 10% year-on-year to Rs 4.8 lakh crore in CY25, indicating consumers' willingness to allocate more wallet share despite record gold prices. However, volumes declined by 15%, reflecting price-sensitive demand shifting preferences towards lower-carat and lighter-weight jewellery, and postponing discretionary purchases. This suggests a resilient market in value but a notable shift in consumer behavior for volume.

viewpoints.title: Gold consumption patterns shift, investment demand set to comprise 35-40% by FY27.
viewpoints.description: Gold consumption patterns are undergoing a structural shift, with jewellery accounting for less than 60% of India's total gold purchases in CY25, down from a long-term average of ~70%. Geopolitical uncertainty, gold price momentum, and portfolio diversification preferences are expected to continue fueling investment demand, projecting its share in overall gold consumption to 35-40% in FY27.

viewpoints.title: Watches face severe pressure in China, declining significantly due to changing consumer preferences.
viewpoints.description: The watches segment in mainland China experienced severe pressure in 2025, with an estimated decline of 14-17%. This was driven by consumers becoming more rational in their purchases, a shift in preferences towards alternative investment assets, the availability of secondhand alternatives, and the growing appeal of sporty and smart-device alternatives. This indicates a challenging environment for traditional watch brands.

viewpoints.title: Jewellery is the standout performer in the global luxury goods market for 2025.
viewpoints.description: In the global personal luxury goods market, jewellery was the standout category across all regions in 2025. Leading players sustained growth through focused clienteling and experiential activations. This positive performance occurred despite intensifying competition in Asia, highlighting jewellery's resilience and appeal compared to other segments like watches and apparel which remained stable or declined.

viewpoints.title: Jewellery and small indulgences are sole positive contributors to personal luxury growth since 2023.
viewpoints.description: Amidst a broad slowdown across soft luxury categories like apparel, leather, and shoes, jewellery and small indulgences (including eyewear and beauty) have emerged as the only positive contributors to the entire personal luxury goods market since 2023. This highlights a significant shift in consumer spending patterns within the luxury sector, favoring items perceived as more enduring or accessible luxury.
